judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Inline SVG co-brand logo 'TUA SAÚDE | REDE D'OR' that heads the footer find-a-doctor nav. The live HTML has no title, aria-label or role on it, and the AX tree exposes it as an unnamed image. The nav's own text (city and insurer links, 'Disponível em...') never says this is a Rede D'Or partner service, so the logo carries information that has no text alternative, which is a 1.1.1 failure. One correction: the message says 'hidden from screen readers', but the SVG is not aria-hidden. It is exposed as an image with no name. The substance of the claim, a meaningful image with no text alternative, still holds.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Newsletter footer input (type=email, name=email, placeholder 'Digite seu email') collects the user's own email address, which is one of the input purposes listed for 1.3.5. Both the snapshot and the live HTML show no autocomplete attribute, so the purpose is not programmatically identified (H98 is not met). Under 1.3.5, type=email alone is not accepted as identifying the purpose. Real failure.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: 'Dúvidas comuns' is the last link in the article's anchor tabs. Site CSS sets .article-anchors ul li a to var(--gray-60) = #8f8f8f on a white background, at 16px weight 400. That is 3.23:1, below the 4.5:1 required. The screenshot shows it as gray text, partly faded under the 'next' gradient button, which only lowers its contrast further. The sibling tab links use the same color, so the measurement is not an artefact. Real 1.4.3 failure.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The newsletter email field's placeholder 'Digite seu email' is #a3a3a3 (var(--gray-50) via .input::placeholder) on the .input white background, 14px weight 400. That is 2.52:1, below 4.5:1. The field has no visible label, so the placeholder is the only on-screen text that says what to type. It is visible text with no 1.4.3 exception (the control is active), so it fails 1.4.3.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the WhatsApp share link in the left share bar: a white WhatsApp glyph on a #25d366 circle (class 'green'). The ratio 1.98:1 is measured correctly. However, #25d366 with a white glyph is WhatsApp's own brand logo presentation. The 1.4.11 Understanding document places logos under the 'essential' exception and says the exemption carries over normatively when the logo is used as a user interface component. Giving it more contrast is only a best practice there. The low contrast comes from the brand colors, not from a design choice by this site, so this is not a 1.4.11 failure as WCAG defines it. The rule applied G207 without the logo exception.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: 'Próximo item' is the scroll button for the article anchor tabs, visible at desktop width; the screenshot shows a small blue '>' caret. Its only visible content is the caret SVG in var(--primary-60) = #36b1df on the button's white gradient over a white page, which is 2.47:1. The caret is the only thing that shows the control is there and what it does, and it is not a logo, so it needs 3:1 under 1.4.11. Real failure.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The header 'Busca IA do Tua Saúde' trigger is a <label for=headerSearch tabindex=0> with click and keydown listeners. The input it points to sits inside a hidden search container, so this label is the only way to open the search overlay. Chrome exposes it as LabelText with an empty computed name and no button or link role. Native labels do not respond to Enter, so the keyboard behavior is scripted. This is a scripted custom control whose role is not programmatically determinable (F59 pattern), so 4.1.2 fails. A <button> or role=button would fix it.
